learn.intro: Real systems mix three tools. Jev gives fast, cheap judgments with typed answers. An LLM writes and reasons in free text. Plain code does exact rules and math. The skill is sending each job to the right one. Sort six task cards, then run them and see what each tool really did.

compare.title: Jev
points: Typed answers: choices, yes or no, scores

compare.title: An LLM
points: Writes and summarizes in free text
Can reason, at a higher cost
Slower, and its format can slip

compare.title: Plain code
points: Exact for rules, math and dates
Needs a rule written in advance

questions.prompt: Across all six jobs, who finishes more of them correctly?

router.title: Sort a support message
router.prompt: Put one support message into billing, technical or account.
router.why: A fast, cheap judgment with a fixed set of labels is exactly what Jev is for.

router.title: Add two numbers
router.why: Arithmetic has one exact answer, so code does it instantly, for free and with no chance of a slip.

router.title: Write a poem
router.prompt: Write four lines about a lighthouse at night.
router.why: Writing new text is System Two work. Jev only returns typed answers.

router.title: Spot a scam message
router.prompt: Decide whether a message is trying to get a password or a payment.
router.why: A yes or no judgment on a message is quick and cheap for Jev, and it also gives a probability.

router.title: Which date is first
router.prompt: Say which of two dates in the format year-month-day comes first.
router.why: Comparing dates that are already structured is a one-line rule. Code is exact and free.

router.title: Summarize a paragraph
router.prompt: Write one sentence that sums up a short news item.
router.why: Condensing text into new words needs generation, which is what an LLM does.

why: No single tool wins every card. Jev took the quick judgments, code took the exact rules, and the LLM took the writing.
Where a tool cannot do a job, the table shows what really happened: Jev rejected the writing requests, and code has no rule for the open-ended ones.
Sorting well is the habit that keeps a system fast, cheap and right.

questions.prompt: Which tool should add up an invoice total?
questions.explanation: Sums have one exact answer. Code gets it every time, instantly and for free.

questions.prompt: What is a good first step in a mixed system?

options.text: Send each job to the tool that fits it

questions.explanation: Fit each job to Jev, an LLM or code. One tool for everything is usually slower, dearer or less exact.
